_comment: ChromeHounds (534507D4) leaderboard property map.
GENERATED FROM THE TITLE'S OWN SPA. Source: one boot with --dump_stats_schema=true (client build
f6f9a019b), captured at workspaces/logs/dump_stats/xenia.log -- 278 stats views parsed by Xenia from the
SPA embedded in the XEX. An earlier revision guessed statIds sequentially and inferred aggregation from
write behaviour; both now come from the title's own declaration. No inference remains in this file.
⚠ KEY FORMAT IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT OBVIOUS. The controller looks properties up by
PropertyId.toString(), which is `0x` + value.toString(16).toLowerCase() -- i.e. LOWERCASE hex with NO
leading zeros. So 0x2000004D must be written 0x2000004d, and 0x00000002 must be written 0x2. A key in any
other form silently fails to match and the property is dropped with 'UNKNOWN STAT ID FOR PROPERTY' -- the
write still 200s, so nothing surfaces except a warning in the server log. An earlier revision of this file
used uppercase, fixed-width keys; twelve of eighteen matched by coincidence (all-digit, 8-wide) and six
were silently discarded until a capture showed the warnings.
statId = the SPA Field ORDINAL. Chosen over attributeId because ordinal is globally stable for a property
across every view, whereas attributeId is view-relative (a property carries the reserved 0xFFFE in the
view where it is the rating column and a numbered id elsewhere) -- and this file must express ONE mapping
for all views. Reserved attribute ids: 0xFFFF Rank, 0xFFFD Gamertag, 0xFFFE Rating.
method comes from the SPA AggregationType enum (xam/xdbf/spa_info.h):
(kMax = 0x800B, kMin = 0x8009 -- neither occurs in this title.)
THE TWO KINDS MATTER, and conflating them silently discards data. Corroborated against the write capture
at workspaces/logs/pilot_rankings/webservices_excerpt.log:
* Last columns arrive as CUMULATIVE career totals. 0x20000044 held 72706 across four consecutive
writes; 0x20000048 climbed 21278 -> 24983. The client accumulates, the server takes the latest.
* Sum columns arrive as PER-MATCH DELTAS. 0x20000050 went 1173 -> 804 -> 855 -> 2046 and 0x2000004D
fell 398 -> 287 -- a decrease is a legitimate negative delta, not a total going backwards. Storing
these with 'set' would keep only the LAST match's delta and discard the career value, on eight
columns, silently, while looking perfectly plausible in the database.
⚠ An earlier note in this file said 'the server stores snapshots, it does not accumulate'. That is true
of the Last columns ONLY. It was derived from fields that happened all to be Last. Do not restate it.
Every view declares exactly ONE rating column (attributeId 0xFFFE) -- the board's sort key, and what a
ranked-query endpoint must order by. See _leaderboards below: 15 boards, view-id <-> name mapping
OPERATOR-VERIFIED by visiting each board in a known order against 30 enumerator calls (15 x ByXUID+ByRank).
THE Last/Sum SPLIT IS SKILL-vs-COUNTER, NOT TOTAL-vs-SEASON. An earlier revision of this file guessed the
latter and it was wrong. The six Last-rated views are exactly the six role-class SKILL Totals -- a skill
LEVEL is a current value, so it is snapshotted. Everything else is Sum: Free Battle and Shots Fired are
COUNTERS, and every Seasonal board accumulates within its season.
⚠ DO NOT DERIVE SEASONAL VIEW IDS FROM TOTAL VIEW IDS. The two groups are ordered differently and only
SOL coincides; a rule fitted to the totals mis-assigns four of the six seasonals. Use the table.
⚠ View 0x0B (Free Battle Total) is arbitrated=1 with only 5 columns, structurally unlike the other 14
18-column views. Its rating property 0x20000006 appears in NO other board -- do not assume the 18-column
shape when handling it.
Ordinal is a safe global statId: no property takes more than one ordinal across the 15 boards. Ordinal 4
is used by BOTH 0x20000006 and 0x20000043, but they never co-occur in a view and storage is per
(leaderboard id, player), so the duplicate is harmless.
Ordinals 0 and 1 (0x10008001 Rank, 0x40008002 Gamer Name) are derived columns the title never writes and
are deliberately NOT mapped; the server supplies rank and gamertag itself.
ARBITRATED VIEWS ARE REPORTED REDUNDANTLY BY DESIGN. Arbitrated stats are a CONSENSUS mechanism: every
session member reports its view of every player's result, and the service compares them before applying
the delta once -- disagreement means the session was tampered with. So Xenia submits arbitrated views from
every console for every player, and duplicate reports are EXPECTED, not a bug.
⚠ 'sum' on the two 0x1000800x entries therefore means sum ACROSS MATCHES, ONCE PER MATCH -- never sum
across the reports received. Applying every report would multiply the delta by the player count on exactly
the columns arbitration exists to protect. The write path enforces this outside this file: the controller
flags arbitrated views (the reserved 0xFFFF0000, plus any view the SPA declares arbitrated via
_leaderboards[].arbitrated) and UpdateLeaderboardCommandHandler claims each (session, view, player) exactly
once through ArbitrationReport's unique index. First report applies; later ones are compared and logged on
mismatch. See ArbitrationReportSchema for the policy and why apply-once was chosen over strict unanimity.
Non-arbitrated views must NOT be de-duplicated: FlushStats sends them incrementally during play and those
repeats are legitimate progressive updates carrying different values.
⚠ The 0x1000800x statIds (100/101) remain arbitrary; nothing in the SPA pins them.
